# setPath

<link-summary>Writes a nested property by path, creating what is missing.</link-summary>

<web-summary>setPath() — Writes a nested property by path, creating what is missing. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/object</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function setPath<T extends object>(
  target: T,
  path: string | Array<string | number>,
  value: unknown
): T;
```

Missing links are created along the way: a numeric segment makes an array, a string segment an object. `setPath({}, ["rows", 0, "id"], 7)` therefore produces `{ rows: [{ id: 7 }] }`.

**The target is modified in place** and returned, so the call composes but does not copy.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                | Description                                       |
| :-------- | :---------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `target`  | `T`                                 | The object to write into. It is modified.         |
| `path`    | `string \| Array<string \| number>` | A dotted string, or an array of keys and indices. |
| `value`   | `unknown`                           | The value to write.                               |

## Returns

`T` — the same object, now carrying the value.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                          |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the target is not an object, or the path is empty. |

## Examples

### Writing

```javascript
setPath({}, "a.b", 1); // => { "a": { "b": 1 } }
setPath({}, ["rows", 0, "id"], 7); // => { "rows": [{ "id": 7 }] }
```
